rawAnswer: {"findings":[{"kind":"defect","severity":"high","title":"Constructor fallback now prefers fewest parameters for all types","detail":"In GetObjectInfo, when no [SerializationConstructor] is present, constructors of equal accessibility are now tried fewest-parameters-first (ThenBy) instead of most-parameters-first (ThenByDescending). The requirement does not ask for this. The fallback loop takes the first constructor whose parameters all match, so a public parameterless constructor now always wins over a full constructor. This change applies to every type, not only suppressed ones, which breaks N2. Generated formatters for existing types that have both constructors will switch to the parameterless one. Get-only or private-set members that the full constructor used to set will then not be restored on deserialization, so data is silently lost. That throws ArgumentNullException, so the analyzer fails with AD0001 and the rest of the type's diagnostics are lost. The property path avoids this with 'else if (stringKey is not null)', but the field path has no such guard and no continue after the null-key diagnostic.
